- .claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md:46 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The `.claude/` conflict PushNotification template hardcodes `<default>` although the sync can merge from the PR's base or a project branch.
  WHY: The notification can name the wrong conflict source and misdirect the operator's investigation.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md:46 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The `.claude/` conflict PushNotification template hardcodes `<default>` although the sync can merge from the PR's base or a project branch.
  WHY: The notification can name the wrong conflict source and misdirect the operator's investigation. Reviewers disagree on severity; the highest severity is high.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:step 2 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: Step 2 does not explicitly direct the agent to continue to step 3 when either check exits non-zero.
  WHY: An agent may interpret the exit condition as terminal success and skip the mandatory merge in step 3.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:186 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Step 2 does not explicitly direct the agent to continue to step 3 when either check exits non-zero.
  WHY: An agent reading step 2 in isolation could stop on a non-zero exit and miss the base-drift-only case.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:lines 187–189 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The instruction "sync the project branch first exactly as step 2 does" does not spell out the checkout, merge, push, and return sequence.
  WHY: An agent on the PR head may run step 2's diffs there instead of updating the project branch, leaving its guard changes stale and causing a blocker loop.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:lines 188–190 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The "Any other base" case does not specify how to handle simultaneous default-drift and base-drift checks exiting non-zero.
  WHY: Merging only `origin/<base>` can leave default-branch guards absent without recording the default-drift signal.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:line 182 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The heading promises two checks although the base-drift check is conditional.
  WHY: A literal reading can lead to a redundant fetch and diff for a default-based PR head or project branch.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:line 189 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The blocker-evidence diff assumes `origin/<project branch>` has already been fetched.
  WHY: On a fresh clone where that ref is unavailable, the diff fails instead of listing the diverging paths.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:line 189 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: If the project-branch fetch fails, the blocker-evidence diff produces a raw Git error rather than the documented structured blocker evidence.
  WHY: A transient fetch failure can leave the operator without the named check and paths in the blocker.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:lines 181, 183, 188; .claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md:46 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The commands use different placeholder names, `<base>` and `<base ref>`, for the same PR base ref concept.
  WHY: Each command works with its own placeholder, but copying prose between them can cause a maintainer to reference a nonexistent remote ref.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

- .claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md: line 46, `PushNotification (`<repo>#<N>: .claude/ conflict with <default> — decision needed`)` | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The PushNotification template hardcodes `<default>` although the sync's merge source can be the default branch, project branch, or PR's own base.
  WHY: During a project-branch or PR-base merge, the notification names `<default>` even though the PR comment names the actual source.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: lines 187–189, step 3, project-branch case ("sync the project branch first exactly as step 2 does") | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The instruction "sync the project branch first exactly as step 2 does" is ambiguous because step 2 only fetches and runs a three-dot diff.
  WHY: An agent on the PR head may not switch to and update the project branch, so its verification keeps failing and can enter a blocker loop.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: lines 188–190, step 3, "Any other base" case ("With base drift, merge `origin/<base>` into the PR head … With default drift only, skip the merge") | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The text does not say what to do when both drift checks exit non-zero on a non-default-bound PR head.
  WHY: After merging `origin/<base>`, the head can still lack default-branch guards, with no stale-base record or explicit instruction for the simultaneous drift.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: line 182, step 2 heading "**Stale?** Two checks, run against the branches the working branch takes its guards from" | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The heading promises two checks although the base-drift check is conditional.
  WHY: A literal reading can cause a redundant fetch and diff per session.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: line 186, step 2 trailing sentence "Both exit 0 → nothing to do." | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: Step 2 only states the success condition and does not direct the agent to step 3 when either check exits non-zero.
  WHY: An agent reading step 2 in isolation could stop and miss the base-drift-only case.
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: line 189, project-branch verification blocker ("naming the check and the paths `git diff --name-only origin/<project branch>...origin/<default> -- .claude/hooks .claude/settings.json` lists") | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The blocker-evidence diff assumes `origin/<project branch>` has already been fetched.
  WHY: If the ref is missing, the diff fails instead of listing the diverging paths.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md and .claude/commands/fix-claude-pr.md: implement-plan-claude.md lines 181, 183, 188 (`<base>`); fix-claude-pr.md line 46 (`<base ref>`) | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The commands use different placeholder names for the same PR-base-ref concept.
  WHY: Copying prose between commands could cause an unrecognised remote ref and lead to the base-drift check being skipped.
